articles.title: US States Sue OpenAI, Citing 'Cyberhacking Agents'
articles.content: At least eight states are suing artificial intelligence giant OpenAI, saying the company’s popular chatbot model violated state consumer protection laws by hurting children and deceiving adults in what prosecutors described as a reckless pursuit of profit. Recommended Video The company’s chatbot model, ChatGPT, is giving dangerous medical advice, encouraging paranoia and coaching people to kill themselves or hurt or kill others, the lawsuits said. At the same time, the lawsuits contend that chatbots are pretending to be agreeable and compassionate while preying on the vulnerable and on teenagers, the first generation to grow up with artificial intelligence . “OpenAI is hurting kids and they are lying to Iowans,” Iowa Attorney General Brenna Bird said in a statement. The states also accused OpenAI of giving life to rogue AI models — or “cyberhacking agents” as one lawsuit called them — that hacked into other companies, lied to human users and wrote themselves new mission instructions. In a statement, San Francisco-based OpenAI said it has built safety protections into ChatGPT for children, and that it would continue to do so to improve the model. It also said it is reviewing what it calls “misaligned models” and that it had found nothing close to the rogue incident discovered in July when an AI agent hacked into another AI company. The wave of lawsuits is the latest filed by states under their consumer protection laws, accusing tech giants that offer AI chatbots and social media platforms of harming children. The states that filed separate lawsuits Wednesday in state courts are Arizona, Arkansas, Idaho, Kansas, Montana, Nebraska and West Virginia. Matthew Bergman, the founding attorney of the Social Media Victims Law Center, called the lawsuits “the most significant coordinated state action ever taken against an artificial intelligence company.” In its lawsuit, Arizona said ChatGPT encourages teens to share personal information with it and, at times, discourages them from sharing that information with parents, authorities or friends. The states say that the risks and harms — to teenagers and to the broader public from rogue agents — were foreseeable, but that OpenAI has misled people into thinking that ChatGPT undergoes adequate safety testing while the company undermines safety in the pursuit of profit. “Those revenues have come at great cost to the public, which has suffered irreparable harm — including lost loved ones, disturbing cyberattacks, and now a plausible threat of civilizational collapse — due to (OpenAI’s) reckless behavior and ChatGPT’s uniquely dangerous features and content,” Idaho wrote in its lawsuit. ChatGPT is the most popular chatbot in the world, commanding nearly half the American marketplace, states said in their lawsuits. It’s possible all of the allegations in the states’ lengthy lawsuits date to incidents and findings before August, when OpenAI introduced a version of ChatGPT designed for teenagers , with stronger protections around subjects like suicide and sexual chats. Still, the states said it is far from clear that the current version is any less dangerous. A watchdog group, Common Sense Media, said last week that some of OpenAI’s protections in its ChatGPT for Teens product don’t work as intended and it urged OpenAI to restrict the chatbot to adults until it can offer a safe product for teens. Coordinated, multistate lawsuits against the tech industry have borne fruit. In August, Meta agreed to add stronger child-safety measures to its Facebook and Instagram platforms in an $18 billion landmark legal settlement that ended a trial over teen social media addiction and settled claims filed by nearly every state. Although the safety measures that Meta agreed to adopt did not apply industrywide, the company quickly urged its competitors to adopt similar measures. OpenAI is making a similar appeal. OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri said the company is committed to working with states on “advancing pragmatic AI policies that apply to the entire AI industry — not just one company.” OpenAI also said it works with external experts who review its policies and ChatGPT’s behavior. ChatGPT is intended for users age 13 and older, and users under 18 need permission from a parent or guardian to use it, OpenAI said. The chatbot model for teens is designed to reduce exposure to self-harm, violence, eating disorders and explicit sexual or graphic content, it said. Nearly nine in 10 teens who use ChatGPT use it for learning, information, skill-building or productivity, the company said. On average, teens spend under 15 minutes a day on ChatGPT, it said. But Laura Zimmermann, Common Sense Media’s director of youth AI research, questioned the value of OpenAI’s statistics. For one thing, ChatGPT can do a student’s homework in seconds, so even 15 minutes can have a big impact on a teenager’s development, Zimmermann said. She also questioned whether OpenAI knows which users are teenagers or children, given that her organization’s testing found that ChatGPT couldn’t or didn’t detect which user is a child. articles.title: Gulf Energy Infrastructure Attacks Raise Global Outlook Concerns
articles.content: Asad HASHIM Oct 17, 2026 Add AL-MONITOR on Google Pakistan’s Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb said the country had procured enough energy supplies to last until November, and was planning future purchases — Lillian SUWANRUMPHA Pakistan's finance minister on Saturday told AFP the country had so far withstood the shock from skyrocketing energy prices due to the Iran war, but that attacks on infrastructure in Saudi Arabia and other Gulf countries were "worrying" for the country's longer-term economic outlook. In an interview on the sidelines of the IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Muhammad Aurangzeb said the South Asian country had procured enough energy supplies to last through November, and was now planning for the winter months, when household needs typically spike. "The first-order impact has been negotiated well by Pakistan," he said. "We've had no shortage, no queues at the gas stations, and no law and order situation, which at times we have seen in some of the countries." He added that unless the government saw "an absolute dire need", it would not be procuring spot cargoes on the LNG front, which tend to be far more expensive than previously contracted shipments. Since the United States and ally Israel launched the war on Iran in February, global energy prices have surged as Tehran's retaliatory action has targeted Washington's Gulf allies and curtailed oil and gas supplies. With Yemen's civil war flaring back to life as well, the Houthis there have repeatedly attacked Saudi infrastructure, including energy facilities and airports, in recent days. Aurangzeb expressed alarm at the escalation, saying damage to such sites would delay a return to economic normalcy. "What is now (the) worrying part of it is when the energy infrastructure starts getting hit," he said. "I, to be very honest, I don't know where that would go. But one thing is very clear: that if the infrastructure continues to get hit, the return to normalcy, even if things subside, will take longer." - 'Pushback' - Pakistan has been a frequent customer at the International Monetary Fund (IMF), the lender of last resort to countries on the brink of default. It is currently in the midst of its 25th programme with the Fund -- at least 11 of which have been outright bailouts -- since gaining independence in 1947. The current programme totals around $7 billion over three years, with the Fund reaching an agreement this month to release a $1.2 billion tranche. With global debt stocks running high, the Fund has called at this year's annual meetings on all economies, even those most vulnerable to the Iran war shock, to engage in fiscal consolidation to avoid a potential crisis. "Fortunately for us, we have been on this fiscal consolidation path for a while," Aurangzeb said with a rueful smile. The country's tax revenues have grown significantly in recent years, and the finance minister said the government was targeting the theft of taxes by private sector businesses that collected sales tax from consumers but never deposited it in government accounts. Such theft accounted for billions of dollars, Aurangzeb said, adding that there remained "room for improvement" on increasing income tax collection as well. He said the government's reform agenda had faced resistance from industry, lobbying groups and vested interests. "Every reform, everything that you try to do when you try to change the status quo, there is pushback," he said. One of the major pillars of the IMF's programme criteria is privatising state-owned assets in Pakistan, where the military runs a vast empire of businesses in sectors from real estate to fertiliser. Asked about those companies, Aurangzeb denied that they were receiving state funding. "As far as we are concerned, whichever commercial enterprises (the military) are running, they are running on a standalone basis and profitable on their own basis," he said. "So, I can confirm to you, we are not providing any funds from the exchequer." Pakistan's military has directly ruled the country for roughly two-fifths of its history, and under current army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir it has tightened its grip over key pillars of power, even as a civilian government remains nominally in charge of the state. aha/hol This one's on us. Ylen MOT:n selvitys paljastaa, että Suomesta on tarjottu merkittävää apua Venäjän sotateollisuudelle. Kaksi Suomen kansalaista ovat myyneet Venäjälle suuria määriä elektroniikkaa. Sitä voidaan hyödyntää esimerkiksi ohjusten osumisessa maaliin. Suomalaisten myymän teknologian avulla voidaan rakentaa ohjusten aivoja. Suomessa ei ole aiemmin paljastunut pakotteiden aikana tämän mittaluokan komponenttien vientiä Venäjälle. Tapaus on maailmanlaajuisestikin harvinainen. MOT vieraili syyskuun lopulla Pohjois-Italiassa Besozzon kylässä. Kansainvälisen verkoston suomalainen päätekijä Denis Emelianov on ostanut itselleen sieltä loma-asunnon. Neuvostoliitossa syntynyt liikemies sai Suomen kansalaisuuden vuonna 2018. Avaa kuvien katselu Emelianov kuvattiin Ylellä vuonna 2023, kun hän antoi Lappeenrannassa toimittajalle haastattelun veitsikaupastaan ja sanoi vastustavansa sotaa. Kuva: Kalle Schönberg / Yle Emelianov asuu Luumäellä Etelä-Karjalassa. Olemme pyytäneet viikkojen ajan häneltä haastattelua kameran edessä, mutta turhaan. Olemme kuitenkin saaneet selville, että hän on viettämässä aikaa Italiassa. Emelianovin asunto sijaitsee aidatulla alueella kukkulan laella. Sieltä aukeavat upeat näkymät Maggiorejärvelle. Vuonna 2023 hän antoi Ylelle haastattelun , jossa sanoi vastustavansa Venäjän sotatoimia Ukrainassa. Emelianov on yrittäjä, jolla on erikoisveitsiä myyvä verkkokauppa ja toimitilat Lappeenrannan keskustassa. Emelianovilla on ollut myös muita bisneksiä. Hänen Hongkongiin rekisteröity yhtiönsä PT Technology Asia on vienyt vuosien ajan Venäjälle elektronisia komponentteja. Liiketoiminta kuitenkin kasvoi pian sen jälkeen, kun Venäjä aloitti hyökkäyssodan Ukrainassa helmikuussa 2022. Emelianovin yritys on toimittanut Venäjälle yli 20 miljoonalla eurolla elektroniikkaa, jota voi käyttää laajasti Venäjän ohjuksissa. Suomesta tällaisia tuotteita ei olisi voinut viedä suoraan Venäjälle EU:n pakotteiden takia. Venäjällä tuotteet päätyivät maan sotateollisuutta palveleville yrityksille. Mustalle listalle joutuminen on iso juttu. Se käytännössä lopetti Emelianovin mahdollisuudet tehdä kauppaa yhdysvaltalaisten yritysten kautta ja rajoitti ylipäätään hänen pääsyään yhdysvaltalaiseen teknologiaan. Bisnes kuitenkin ehti olla hänelle tuottoisaa. Ennen Venäjän hyökkäyssotaa hänen ansiotulonsa Suomessa olivat muutamia kymmeniä tuhansia euroja. Komponenttikaupan kiihdyttyä Emelianovin verotettavat tulot nousivat satoihin tuhansiin euroihin. Emelianov matkustelee somepäivitystensä perusteella ympäri maailmaa. articles.title: US Resumes Intelligence Sharing with Ukraine
articles.content: Oct 18 (Reuters) - The United States has resumed providing Ukraine with critical intelligence to help it defend against Russian missile strikes, after a brief pause, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said in comments published on Sunday. By Reuters 18 Oct 2026 epaselect epa10605911 Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelensky arrives to meet his Finnish counterpart Sauli Niinisto President of Finland (not pictured) in Helsinki, Finland, 03 May 2023. Zelenskiy arrived in Finland on Wednesday for meetings with Nordic leaders to discuss the war with Russia and European relations. EPA-EFE/KIMMO BRANDT Dive Deeper Speed Read Listen Dive Deeper Ukraine has relied on US intelligence to spot the fast-moving ballistic missiles that Russia has fired in waves at its cities. US President Donald Trump had said earlier this week that Washington was still sharing intelligence, despite Ukrainian officials saying some Russian strikes had occurred without warning. Speaking to NBC's Meet the Press, Zelenskiy said intelligence-sharing had been interrupted but later "de-blocked". "We are very thankful for this," he said. "Now it works." But Zelenskiy said that other US actions, such as signing a deal to import Russian diesel and waiving sanctions on Russia that had been slated to take effect this week, will hurt Ukraine. "If the United States will officially take the side of Russia, of course if these two countries will be together, of course we will not prevail and we will not be able to stand," he said. Over the past week, a widening rift between Trump and Zelenskiy has sparked concerns that their tumultuous relationship could ​lead to even worse outcomes for Kyiv. Zelenskiy told NBC that he hopes Trump will remain an ally of Ukraine. "We want to trust him, and I hope that he will change his decisions," Zelenskiy said. "Because I think that it's all mistakes and it will not help us. And it will not help United States." Ukraine gets US help that Russia does not receive, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told NBC, citing intelligence-sharing and the provision of US munitions to other countries for resale to Ukraine. But Bessent, speaking with "Meet the Press" after it aired Zelenskiy's interview, did not directly answer when asked multiple times whether the United States views Ukraine as an ally. "Zelenskiy presents a false binary this morning that Ukraine must win," Bessent said. "The war must end, and that will be with some kind of a negotiated settlement." (Reporting by Dan Peleschuk and Michael Derby; Editing by Joe Bavier, Sergio Non and Edmund Klamann) World

articles.title: AI CEO Limits Access to Prevent 'Dumbening' Effects
articles.content: LivestreamMenuPaysend CEO Ben Chisell limits access to general-purpose AI tools to high-performing employees who can show what the tools add.Lloyds Banking Group and Grant Thornton UK are among companies deploying AI tools broadly across their workforces.U.K. government research found 75% of AI-using businesses reported improved workforce productivity, but 77% reported no revenue change.Laurence Dutton | E+ | Getty ImagesAt London-headquartered payments technology company Paysend, access to artificial intelligence tools has to be earned.CEO Ben Chisell told CNBC he is a “very cynical man” about the hype around the technology, though he still sees value in it. Chisell, who previously worked at Amazon, eBay and Starling Bank, estimates that Paysend can now deliver around 25% more engineering work with the same-sized team, but argues that getting results isn’t as simple as handing everyone the latest tech. Instead, he limits AI tools to his highest-performing employees, often only after they’ve proved what they can do with them. In the wrong hands, he said, AI can magnify bad habits such as laziness and poor judgment. His broader rule is to resist the “fear of missing out” and focus on customer problems. “I know it sounds very unglamorous and unsexy as an approach given the world of tokenmaxxing and AI, but I think it’s really, really important,” Chisell said. The pressure to demonstrate AI’s value is growing, from the legal sector to software engineering and finance, and many companies are responding by putting the technology in as many hands as possible. London-based Lloyds Banking Group has rolled out 40,000 Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses, with 97% of employees who have one actively using it, the bank said. Newcastle-headquartered software company Sage said its AI coding tools had saved hundreds of thousands of work hours, while London-based professional services firm Grant Thornton UK has encouraged all of its staff to use Anthropic’s Claude as part of a £500 million ($660 million) investment in AI. These figures do not necessarily translate into gains on the bottom line, however. U.K. government research published in January found that three-quarters of businesses using AI said it had improved workforce productivity, but 77% said revenue had not changed. Like Chisell, Lokdeep Singh, CEO of British enterprise software company Unily, sees AI as a “superpower” best reserved for high-performing employees. He is also wary of companies giving it out to everyone as a way to reduce costs. “I personally believe you should use it to expand your ambition rather than make the team smaller,” he told CNBC. “But the reality is that in many industries, again, because of the macro environment, it is being thought as: ‘OK, can I cut costs? Can I cut employees?’ The truth is probably somewhere in between.” At Paysend, Chisell wants employees to demonstrate what a tool actually contributes. New hires get a month to experiment with AI tools and explain what they have achieved. He recently put that policy to the test with a new search engine optimization lead who requested access to Claude. A month later, the employee told Chisell he no longer needed it. All he found it useful for, he said, was producing briefs more quickly. So instead of a general-purpose AI tool, the employee suggested building a dedicated content-brief agent, which he is now working on. At software company CoreView, the approach has been different. London-based CEO Simon Azzopardi told CNBC the company was initially “very gung-ho” on AI, initiating a widespread rollout for its software engineers. They first used AI to investigate problems by correlating logs, events and data, as well as to produce technical documentation and onboard new engineers faster. Now, he said, developers increasingly coordinate teams of AI agents handling tasks including back-end and front-end coding, quality assurance and documentation. Azzopardi said work that previously took weeks could now take days. However, AI-generated work isn’t necessarily productive if employees use it to build things outside their expertise, Azzopardi warned. “You feel more efficient, but you actually aren’t,” he said. Still, when onboarding a major customer in the U.K.’s National Health Service, CoreView only needed to add one engineer while continuing to deliver its other projects, he said. The company has been hiring rather than cutting staff, using the extra capacity to take on more work. As AI takes on more of people’s existing responsibilities, the question is what happens to the employees who used to do these tasks. Chisell believes companies will thrive if they help employees move into new roles, rather than replace them once their work is automated. Customer-service workers, for example, have spent years resolving complex issues — a skill that’s valuable across a business, he said. For Chisell, technology should never replace human responsibility. “Having a human in the loop shouldn’t mean human CC’d,” he said. “It should mean human ownership.”

articles.title: Apple's HomeView Battles Google for Smart Home Dominance
articles.content: As someone who’s kept a smart display on the kitchen counter for the last eight years, I should be among the target audience for Apple HomeView. My Lenovo Smart Display is one of the best gadgets I’ve ever owned, mainly because it’s always cycling through family photos that I’d otherwise surely forget. In addition to being a constant source of fond memories for me and my family, it is also occasionally useful for kitchen timers, music, weather forecasts, and managing the grocery list. HomeView , which launches next month for $299, brings an Apple-like layer of polish to the smart display concept, with a high-resolution display, aluminum base, and built-in subwoofer. Its facial recognition capabilities also allow it to display each person’s messages and calendar events. But for all those bells and whistles, HomeView appears to fall short on the one feature I care about most: Its photo features are designed around iCloud Photos, making it a tough sell for me and the other 1.5 billion people who use Google Photos . Without a steady supply of fresh photos, HomeView might wind up feeling a bit empty. Those who’ve seen the HomeView up close liken it to a giant Apple Watch , with a 7-inch square-shaped screen that provides information at a glance. The main “Faces” view cycles through things like the time, weather, and photos, and you can swipe up to a home screen for built-in apps and smart home controls. At least at the outset, the emphasis is clearly on Apple apps and services such as FaceTime, Apple Music, Podcasts, and Safari. The role for third-party apps is more limited. If a music or video app is compatible with CarPlay, Apple’s in-vehicle projection system, Apple may provide similar access on HomeView when a compatible iPhone is nearby. This would allow users to access third-party music like Spotify. HomeView will also support third-party home screen widgets , similar to those on iOS. As for photos, Apple hasn’t gone into much detail, other than saying it will offer “Portrait-style depth effects” and support for shared albums that “loved ones near and far can help fill.” Smart displays from Google and Amazon are both able to surface photos of specific people, including new photos that users upload to cloud storage over time, so hopefully that will be a possibility with HomeView as well. Either way, Apple has not announced any provisions for displaying photos from outside its own ecosystem. Its photo frame features will likely rely on users’ iCloud Photos libraries exclusively. Although some folks have wondered about the HomeView’s target audience , I’ve always felt that photo frames are the ideal use case for a smart display. It’s a frictionless way to revisit all the smartphone photos you’ve taken, and it fits perfectly with the concept of a communal device for everyone in the home. Compared to stand-alone digital photo frames, I also like that these devices can do a little bit more, such as controlling smart home devices, playing music, and setting timers. Without the photo component, though, a device like HomeView just becomes another screen in a home already filled with them. Using it as a photo frame is what justifies everything else. For me, at least, HomeView won’t be of much use if I can’t bring my Google Photos library with me. While Google does offer an easy way to transfer your entire Google Photos library to iCloud Photos , I’d rather not switch photo systems just for the sake of a new gadget. Besides, I prefer Google Photos anyway as someone who doesn’t exclusively use Apple products . To be fair, other smart displays are similarly closed-off to third-party photo sources. Google’s Nest Hub is for Google Photos, and Amazon’s Echo Show devices are for Amazon Photos. It’s not surprising that Apple would go the same route, because supporting other sources would create complications, and the whole point of HomeView is to reinforce Apple’s own ecosystem of services. Still, my hope is that over time, Apple will expand the HomeView’s “Faces” feature to third-party apps. That way, alternative providers like Google Photos, Facebook, OneDrive, Ente Photos, and even the self-hosted Immich could provide a showcase for users’ photo libraries. articles.content: Helsinki havittelee kahdesta kolmeen uutta datakeskusta alueelleen. Helsingin kaupunginhallitus käsittelee periaatteita datakeskuksille eli konesaleille maanantaina. Se jätti suunnitelmat pöydälle kesällä. Nyt kaupunginhallitus käsittelee datakeskuslinjauksia uudelleen. Tarkoitus on pohtia tarkemmin energiajärjestelmän kestävyyttä, sähkön riittävyyttä ja luontoon sekä ympäristöön kohdistuvien vaikutusten ehkäisyä. Mahdollisia datakeskusten rakennuspaikkoja olisivat Heikinlaakso, Salmisaari, Malmi, Myllypuro ja Östersundom. Suurmetsän Heikinlaaksoon on jo haettu kehittämisvarausta datakeskushankkeelle. Suunnittelualue on noin 7,3 hehtaarin kokoinen, Kääpätien ja Lahdenväylän välissä. Alueelle suunnitellaan jopa 30 metriä korkeaa datakeskusrakennusta. Kaupungin järjestämään kerro kantasi -kyselyyn vastanneista yli 800 vastaajasta suurin osa vastusti hanketta muun muassa lähiluonnon tuhoutumisen ja sähkönkulutuksen lisääntymisen vuoksi. Avaa kuvien katselu Kuva: Ruuti Kotkanoja / Yle, Mapcreator, OpenStreetMap Datakeskukset tarvitsevat paljon sähköä, ja niiden toiminta nostaa sähkön hintaa. Kaupunginhallituksen käsittelyyn tulevassa ehdotuksessa todetaan, että kantaverkkoyhtiö Fingridin mukaan lähivuosina sähköverkko mahdollistaa vain niukasti uusia investointeja. Esityksen mukaan 2020-luvun lopulle mentäessä tilanne paranee, kun Fingridin investoinnit kaksinkertaistavat liitettävyyskapasiteetin. Hankkeelle ei myönnetä liittymissopimusta, jos sähkön siirtokapasiteettia ei ole riittävästi saatavilla. Helsingin sähkönkulutuksen arvioidaan kasvavan lähivuosina voimakkaasti – vuoteen 2030 mennessä jopa kaksinkertaistuvan vuodesta 2024 – sähköistyvän lämmityksen, liikenteen, satamatoimintojen ja datakeskusten vuoksi. Kaupungin mukaan datakeskukset tuovat yksityisiä investointeja Helsinkiin ja niiden positiivinen vaikutus talouteen näkyy merkittävien tuottojen muodossa. Datakeskukset tuottavat myös hukkalämpöä, jota voisi hyödyntää kaupunkilaisten lämmöntuotannossa. Tavoitteena on mahdollistaa noin 350 megawattitunnin suuruisen lämpömäärän hyödyntäminen vuoteen 2035 mennessä ja noin 500 megawattituntia vuoteen 2040 mennessä. Tämä tukisi Helsingin kaupunkistrategista tavoitetta irtautua polttoon perustuvasta energiantuotannosta vuoteen 2040 mennessä. Datakeskuksista saatavalla lämmöllä voidaan korvata öljyyn, maakaasuun ja biomassaan perustuvaa lämmöntuotantoa. Lisäksi lämmön tuotantoon käytettävää sähkön siirto- ja tuotantokapasiteettia vapautuu muuhun käyttöön, esityksessä todetaan. Kaupungin mukaan datakeskuksia tarvitaan digitaalisiin palveluihin, pilviteknologiaan ja tiedon käsittelyyn. Kun datan määrä lisääntyy, kasvaa myös globaali kysyntä ja tarve uusille konesaleille. articles.title: Anthropic Gives AI Watchdog 'Employee-Like' Access
articles.content: Text settings Story text Size Small Standard Large Width * Standard Wide Links Standard Orange * Subscribers only    Learn more Minimize to nav Anthropic has granted external evaluators “employee-like access” to assess the risks of its models, following through on a commitment to increase safeguards over concerns the technology could run catastrophically out of control. METR, a nonprofit that has worked with leading labs including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta, now has a team embedded in the Claude maker’s office with access to its hardware and internal systems. A greater role for third-party evaluators is among the main concrete steps the labs have proposed in response to rising concern about the dangers more capable AI systems could pose to the economy, cyber security and humanity at large. Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei achieved a rare moment of unity with arch-rivals Sam Altman and Elon Musk in September when the OpenAI and SpaceX bosses rallied behind his proposal to embed external auditors in the leading labs. Thursday’s announcement marks the first step to implementing these pledges. OpenAI has yet to lay out plans to bring in evaluators after Altman said Amodei’s proposals were a good idea. “As models have become more powerful, they’ve required stronger safeguards and more challenging risk assessment,” Anthropic said on Thursday. “We want to be publicly accountable for the decisions we’re making. But we can’t publicly share all the information relevant to our safety work.” Critics of Anthropic’s proposal to use evaluators have argued the arrangements could lead to conflicts of interest, pointing to issues in the accounting sector, and that greater government regulation is required. Anthropic argued that sharing information publicly could benefit malicious actors or competitors and added that its evaluators will operate similarly to bank supervision, whereby regulators assign resident examiners to work inside the largest banks. “If a bank’s risk-taking could threaten the public, third parties try to see that in advance,” the company said. Anthropic is also under pressure to reassure investors that safety issues will not overshadow its initial public offering, expected this year at a more than $2tn valuation. It devoted a large part of investor presentations this week to laying out its safety practices. METR was one of the organisations that investigated the hack of Hugging Face by rogue OpenAI models, reviewing thousands of logs and receiving company laptops. Anthropic has now onboarded six METR employees, giving them company hardware, office space and “access to internal tools and systems that are roughly on par with what our own risk assessment teams have access to.” The lab said it has encouraged employees to share information with the evaluators as they would with a fellow employee working in risk. Anthropic is not paying METR for this arrangement. The research group does not accept donations from AI companies or their staff. It is funded by donations from individuals and philanthropic organisations, as well as government bodies such as the UK’s AI Security Institute. The evaluators will publish their analysis, and Anthropic cannot veto publication. However, it can require them to redact information that falls into certain categories, such as customer data, details covered by attorney-client privilege or information about model architectures. Anthropic added it was still working with Accenture, which was named a partner on safety testing last month, with each committing at least $1 billion to set up new safeguards. Another third-party tester is SecureBio, which reviews chemical and biological weapon risk for the company. “We’re embedding evaluators voluntarily, and we believe every frontier AI company should do the same,” Anthropic said. METR said: “We stand ready to work with all frontier AI developers to bring better evidence to the public.” © 2026 The Financial Times Ltd . articles.title: Writers Warn of AI Training on Music Rights
articles.content: Nick Cave and Kylie Minogue making a video for their duet, Where the Wild Roses Grow, in 1995. They are among Australian artists whose music has been used to train AI. Photograph: Dave Tonge/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Nick Cave and Kylie Minogue making a video for their duet, Where the Wild Roses Grow, in 1995. They are among Australian artists whose music has been used to train AI. Photograph: Dave Tonge/Getty Images Kylie Minogue songs already used to train AI as tech firms ‘strong-arm’ Australian government, music body warns Of the dozens of countries approached to water down their laws, Australia appears to be the only one considering it, publishers’ group says Get our new political email , free app or daily news podcast AI has already been trained on the works of Australian artists including Kylie Minogue and Nick Cave without compensation, the peak global body for music rights has claimed, as the Australian government has been warned against giving in to “strong-arming” from tech companies seeking to weaken copyright law. The International Confederation of Music Publishers (ICMP) – which represents Sony, Warner and Universal as well as thousands of independent publishers on six continents – has warned that of the dozens of countries approached to water down copyright laws, Australia appears to be the only to consider doing so. John Phelan, the ICMP’s managing director, told Guardian Australia AI companies were asking policymakers to “legitimise larceny”. David Pocock concerned senior Albanese adviser ‘vetted’ bipartisan AI letter that was sent to PM Read more “They’re trying to strong-arm Australian policymakers into ‘if you don’t do this, we won’t invest’.” In July, Anthony Albanese said it would be “theft” if artists did not retain control over whether their work was used to build and train AI, and what they were paid for its use. Music, film, media and news organisations had expressed concerns the government was being lobbied by global tech companies behind closed doors to weaken Australia’s copyright laws to help train AI models, without compensating the creative sectors. But government and opposition members of a parliamentary committee on artificial intelligence appeared to revisit the issue this week, describing the current situation as a stalemate. Sign up for Guardian Australia’s Politics, really newsletter here They said AI models were already training on copyrighted works in the United States without compensating creators – but that without changes to local copyright laws, those companies were withholding training frontier AI models in Australia. In a joint letter to the prime minister this week, the inquiry’s Labor chair, Jo Briskey, and its deputy chair, Liberal senator Jonathon Duniam, recommended the government “examine current copyright settings” while ensuring creators retain control and are paid. The independent senator David Pocock has raised concerns that the committee was coming to a position on copyright predetermined by the prime minister, after staffer edits were seen in the letter. Briskey has rejected the claim. AI companies’ demands The ICMP has been tracking how AI companies are attempting to change copyright law in different jurisdictions to allow training. Phelan highlighted methods that the companies had used to train their models on music, such as with spreadsheets containing millions of lines of music available on YouTube. A key claim of the AI industry is that its models are not trained on Australian content due to copyright rules. However, in evidence provided exclusively to Guardian Australia, ICMP showed Google’s Gemini was able to reproduce lyrics from Australian artists including Kylie Minogue, G-Flip and Nick Cave . Phelan also pointed to an AI training dataset reported by the Atlantic in June , which contains more than 12m songs pulled from YouTube videos, including tracks from Minogue, Cave and Hilltop Hoods. Google was approached for comment. Phelan said 62 countries had considered making their own legal changes but none of the others had bought into AI companies’ demands. skip past newsletter promotion after newsletter promotion “There isn’t a single country among the other 61 [countries] … which has introduced a new text and data mining exception for commercial purposes, or reduce the idea of exclusive rights and copyright,” Phelan said. “The world is very much watching what Australia does.” “It’s fair to say the global music industry, as well as all creative industries worldwide we work with, are appalled by the idea of a statutory scheme or a government deal which would interfere with how Australian industries work and contract around the world.” Anthropic’s special envoy, Jeffrey Bleich, told the AI committee last week the company was not trying to dictate terms, but had shared information with the Australian government about training and what the implications would be “with respect to our capacity to operate here”. “You can’t license the entire internet. Billions and billions of information exists there which is available to be viewed and studied, and that’s essentially what training is,” he said. “Under existing Australian law , it’s our understanding that that could be determined to be illegal if we weren’t able to find a licence with every single person who had rights within Australia.” OpenAI’s chief of economic policy, Adam Cohen, said the fair use exception in US law “fundamentally protects” the development of new technology. He pointed to agreements made with News Corp and the Guardian as examples of where the company makes deals for the use of work, despite arguing US law did not require such. Phelan said he believed panic had set in among the AI companies over the sheer cost of investment and the need to make a return, coupled with the ongoing litigation over copyright in the US. He said they may be looking to Australia for a legislative solution. “They’re seeing the legislative side as being the way to try to [find] a place to do business without licences, which will secure their future business model.” In a submission to the inquiry, Guardian Australia said that undermining copyright protection would have a “profound impact on civil society” and copyright-protected material should only be available for AI training with the rights holder’s explicit prior authorisation. articles.title: Mexican Judge Sentences Surfers' Killers to 158 Years
articles.content: How a harrowing trial of two murdered Australian surfers ended in a guilty verdict A Mexican judge has sentenced three men convicted of murdering Australian brothers Jake and Callum Robinson and their US friend Carter Rhoad to 158 years and nine months in jail each. The Robinsons and Rhoad were killed in an apparent botched robbery of their truck on a secluded beach in Baja California in 2024 while they were on a surfing trip, the court heard during the trial. The murders sent shockwaves around the world, particularly in Australia, as the area is usually safe from the violence seen in other parts of Mexico. The guilty verdict was handed down last week. Debra Robinson, the brothers' mother, told the courtroom that her sons' murders had taken "the future we had imagined with them". articles.title: Philippines Navigates Aging Population Crisis in Asia
articles.content: Maria Esperanza Carmen Liamco, 68, once worked overseas on Bahrain’s national ID system and helped found the Philippine School Bahrain. In 1997, after 14 years abroad, she returned to the Philippines to care for her sick mother. Back home, she went on to work in several government offices over 13 years, eight of which as a contractual. But when she retired at 65 (the mandated government retirement age) in 2023, she did not receive any pension. The Government Service Insurance System (GSIS) requires at least 15 years of service for a consistent annual pension, and otherwise provides a flat payout — a sum that, for Liamco, has nearly run dry. After retiring, she returned to work as a board secretary of the school in Bahrain, which supports her. She has savings, and the family owns their Quezon City home, so rent isn’t a worry. But she has concerns about what the unexpected costs of aging could mean for her — for one, medical treatment that could be expensive can wipe out whatever funds she has. Liamco is one of 7.4 million Filipinos aged 65 or older, a group set to grow as Filipino women have fewer children than at any point on record. This shift, experts said, is moving the country toward a new demographic reality: an aging society. The Philippines, long defined by its large share of young people, is at the start of that transition. The United Nations (UN) considers a country an "aging society" once 7% of its population are 65 or older. The population of Filipinos aged 65 and above has seen a steady and significant increase over the past three decades. About 6.6% of Filipinos, or 7.4 million people, are now aged 65 or older, according to the Philippine Statistics Authority's (PSA’s) 2024 census. The Commission on Population and Development (CPD) expects the country to cross over the line by 2028. The question is not whether the Philippines will age: it's what the country does with the time it has left before it does. "The Philippines reached a [fertility rate] of 1.7 at a gross national income per capita of only [P280,450] in 2024, well below the income levels at which most aging societies began their transition," Jose Ramon Albert, a senior research fellow at the Philippine Institute for Development Studies (PIDS), said. "This is the risk of growing old before growing rich." The country’s fertility rate is below the 2.1 total fertility rate needed to keep a population stable, known as "replacement level." Japan has maintained the highest proportion of older persons in the region, while South Korea exhibits the most rapid aging trajectory over the last three decades. Affluent Asian countries like Japan and South Korea reached that point decades earlier, said Albert. Japan fell below replacement level in the mid-1970s and South Korea in the early 1980s. Far from where the Philippines is now, Japan’s gross national income per capita was P1 million when it became an aging society in 1970, while South Korea’s was about P1.4 million in 2000, adjusted for inflation. The effect of a fertility rate below replacement level takes time to show up. The Philippines still added about 3.7 million people between 2020 and 2024, because a large generation of women is still in their childbearing years. That window is closing. In the decades ahead, fewer births mean fewer young workers. As more people retire or leave work than young people enter it, and as people live longer, fewer workers are left to support the nation’s economy. That also puts pressure on older Filipinos to keep working, many with no choice. "The most urgent thing people are usually worried about with aging populations is the workforce shrinking," said Dr. Marie Ng, an associate professor at the National University of Singapore's Yong Loo Lin School of Medicine, who studies demographic and health trends across Asia. "With the workforce shrinking, you also don't have enough of the financial foundation to support the aging needs," she added. Out of every 100 older Filipinos, 42 do not receive any form of pension to support them in their twilight years. Unlike wealthier nations where retirees rely on robust pension systems, millions of aging Filipinos in the informal economy are aging without formal safety nets. 42% of Filipinos aged 60 and older, just like Liamco, have no pension at all. About four million indigent seniors receive P1,000 a month in support and nearly one-third of Social Security System (SSS) pensioners get less than P3,000. Japan's working-age population (people 15 to 64) peaked at about 87 million in 1995 and has since fallen to about 73.5 million. Roughly three in 10 Japanese are now 65 or older, the highest share of any country with a population over 100,000. The overall population has shrunk for 17 consecutive years. Tokyo has spent more than three decades trying to reverse the trend, including a pledge of about ¥3.5 trillion a year (roughly P1.6 trillion) since 2024. Its fertility rate still fell to a record 1.14 in 2025. Adult diapers now outsell ones for babies, and the country has over 9 million vacant homes. South Korea is on a similar path. In 2024, its working-age population fell below 70% of the total population for the first time. After spending an estimated P17.5 trillion over 18 years to boost births, South Korea still has gaps in emergency care and too few neonatal doctors for its already small number of newborns. Its fertility rate is 0.80, among the lowest in the world. The money in both nations has gone into a wide range of measures. Many are aimed at births, such as cash for new parents, better-paid parental leave, and housing help for young families. Pronatal incentives, or efforts to encourage an increase in the births of children, "are not shooting up the fertility rate at all," said Ng. That does not make them worthless. They matter for children's well-being and women's workforce participation, she said, even if they cannot necessarily reverse a decline in population growth. Even with deep pockets, Japan and South Korea have seen limited results. What does that mean for countries with less money? “The current systems in Asia, in general, are not quite ready in terms of the influx of aging populations,” said Ng. The pattern isn’t limited to rich countries. Thailand became an aging society in 2004 with a gross national income per capita of P281,184, according to UN and World Bank data. In 2025, just 416,514 babies were born there, the fewest since 1950, and deaths outnumbered births by more than 143,000. Vietnam is not far behind. It entered its aging transition in 2015 and is projected to become an aged society by the mid-2030s, according to the World Bank, when 14% of its population will be 65 or older. Across Asia, a 2024 Asian Development Bank report found, 40% of people over 60 have no pension, and about 60% don’t get regular health checks. Among workers 65 and older, 94% are in the informal sector. Many Filipinos are no different: workers who are contractuals or in informal jobs have no pension and little savings. As they age, many will have to lean on a stretched public health system and on their children. But there will be fewer children to lean on. The Philippines is one of the world's largest exporters of labor too. At least 10.8 million Filipinos live abroad, and an estimated 2.1 million are overseas workers. Their remittances prop up many households as well as the country’s economy. Albert argued that this also complicates the country's aging timeline in a way none of its neighbors face. "Aging here will unfold alongside a large diaspora, which cushions household incomes through remittances," he said, "but also means that some of the working-age population supporting our elderly will be abroad, and that our care workers are in demand overseas precisely when we will need them at home." It is an irony hard to miss. Many Filipino healthcare workers and caregivers look after other countries' older people abroad. Meanwhile, Filipino children with parents working overseas are cared for by grandparents. When those grandparents need care themselves, who will be there? "Aging is going to be inevitable," Ng said. “And we do expect from data that people will live longer. The question is how to keep people alive, healthy, and productive?" In the Philippines, the question of meeting the moment comes down to being able to retrofit existing systems for its seniors. As Liamco thinks about the future, she said the Philippines needs more long-term solutions for supporting its seniors. “Dole-out programs like bundles of food or funds are good, but we need more proactive efforts and opportunities, especially for seniors who are in more labor jobs who have less support,” she said. The CPD released the Philippine Population and Development Plan of Action (PPD-POA) for 2023-2028, which includes a portion dedicated to fostering a healthy and productive workforce as the population ages. The National Commission of Senior Citizens (NCSC) has a plan for the same period, Philippine Plan of Action for Senior Citizens 2023-2028. Some of their provisions include improving health infrastructure, creating long-term insurance policies, and increasing anti-poverty and social programs for seniors. Scattered data is a hurdle for planning, the office of NCSC Commissioner Gloria-Jumamil Mercado said in a written response to Rappler. Information on seniors is spread across agencies such as the PSA, the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), GSIS, and SSS. “Although the DSWD/PSA has an existing Community-Based Monitoring System (CBMS)/Census, its limitation is timely and accurate record-keeping because it is only updated every three years, causing severe data latency,” said the office. A proposed Philippine Ageing Data Observatory at the NCSC could bring that information into one database, with dashboards, more timely data and real-time analytics down to the local level, according to documents shared with Rappler. The proposal, sponsored by Commissioner Camilo G. Gudmalin, is still subject to deliberation by the Commission en banc. Albert argued the Philippines still has the advantage of time. Its working-age population is still rising, even as the number of births decreases and people age. His prescription: raise the productivity of the country's smaller, incoming generations and broaden pension coverage to informal workers and overseas Filipinos. He also suggested extending healthy working lives through preventive care and building long-term care infrastructure, an effort that presents a serious challenge, given existing basic gaps in healthcare across the country. "The demographic future of the Philippines is already visible in the 2025 National Demographic and Health Survey," Albert said. "Whether we become a development success story depends on whether we treat the next 20 years as the window in which to invest in children and build for aging, rather than as a reprieve." – with reports from Eirene Manatlao/Rappler.com Coding for this layout was done with the assistance of AI.

articles.title: Selma Blair Denies Intent to Harm in Plane Altercation
articles.content: Image source, Getty ImagesByNardine SaadUS actress Selma Blair has spoken out after being accused of assaulting multiple people on a flight to New York. A publicist for the Legally Blonde star said she "did not intend to harm anyone" and that there was "much more to this story". Blair "experienced a medical emergency on the flight" and is still fighting ​multiple sclerosis (MS), a statement read. Blair's publicist said that the 54-year-old had a neurological disorder that "bears directly on how a medical episode presents to people who do not know her". The star pleaded not guilty to charges that she assaulted an officer and a nurse after being removed from the flight. She was also accused of assaulting two flight attendants on board. Blair's team said the public account of what happened to her aboard a Delta Airlines flight to New York had been "built almost entirely on a police statement and a decade-old headline". They also denied media reports that she had attempted to open the door of the aircraft. The publicist noted Blair's fight against multiple sclerosis (MS), a chronic illness the actress revealed publicly in 2018. She announced in 2021 that she was in remission for the disease, but the statement noted that the Hellboy and Cruel Intentions star "still has bad days". It added that she also has pseudobulbar affect (PBA) - a disorder that develops in the context of a brain injury or underlying neurological dysfunction, according to the US National Institutes of Health. The disorder affects emotional expression that can result in sudden involuntary and out-of-control episodes of laughing, crying or anger that do not match how a person actually feels. Watch: Selma Blair is seen leaving court after plane incident Blair's publicist described the actress's physical achievements since her MS diagnosis as "nothing short of a miracle" and said she still lives with pain daily. "Selma had never been arrested before Sunday night," she said. "There is much more to this story than has been reported and we ask to consider the entirety of the facts before rushing to judgement, whether in the courtroom or in the court of public opinion." The incident happened on a flight travelling from Los Angeles to New York on Sunday evening. New York airport officials responded to a call about "a physically abusive passenger" on a Delta Airlines flight. Two flight attendants were hurt and one was taken to hospital, the New York Port Authority said. A pilot asked for medical help, describing "a bloody nose" and "some bite marks", according to audio recorded on air traffic control obtained by CBS News, the BBC's US partner. Blair was arrested and taken to hospital. She was issued a federal summons by the FBI for a charge of assault within the special maritime and territorial jurisdiction of the US that relates to the on-board altercation. The two additional charges of assault were filed in state court after she was taken off the plane. She has pleaded not guilty to those charges and was released on bail.

articles.title: Roborock Qrevo S Pro: Budget Robot Vac Gets Smart
articles.content: ab 389,98 EUR Stefan Schomberg Stefan schrieb bereits während des Studiums Spieletests für ein Printmagazin im Ruhrgebiet. Durch einen glücklichen Zufall landete er in Berlin und arbeitete fast 15 Jahre bei Areamobile, zuletzt als leitender Testredakteur. Für Heise Bestenlisten testet er Smartphones, Saug- und Mähroboter, Lautsprecher, Modellflugzeuge und andere Technik-Gadgets. Der Qrevo S Pro saugt und wischt Hartböden gut und wäscht seine Mopps heiß. Bei Hindernissen, hohen Teppichen und der Randreinigung zeigt er dagegen Schwächen. Der Roborock Qrevo S Pro positioniert sich unterhalb der teuren Spitzenmodelle des Herstellers. Gegenüber dem Vorgänger QV 35A steigt die nominelle Saugkraft deutlich auf 18.500 Pa. Neu sind außerdem die Moppwäsche mit bis zu 75 °C heißem Wasser und die Trocknung mit 45 °C warmer Luft. Unverständlich für einen Mittelklasse-Saugroboter: Weder Seitenbürste noch rechter Mopp können zum Rand hin ausfahren. Wir haben im Test überprüft, wie gut das Modell im Alltag trotzdem ist. Der Qrevo S Pro bleibt beim klassischen Aufbau vieler älterer Roborock Modelle. Der runde Roboter misst etwa 35 cm im Durchmesser und ist am feststehenden Laserturm knapp 10 cm hoch. Damit gehört das Modell nicht zur besonders flachen Klasse aktueller Roboter mit einziehbarer Navigation oder Starsight-System. Unter dem Roboter sitzt eine durchgehende Hauptbürste aus Vollgummi. Sie lässt sich gut reinigen, da sie ohne Borsten auskommt, in denen sich Haare besonders leicht festsetzen können. Ergänzt wird sie durch eine asymmetrisch geformte Seitenbürste, die Haarverwicklungen reduzieren soll. Der Staubbehälter im Roboter fasst 330 ml. Hinzu kommt ein kleiner interner Wassertank mit 80 ml. Die Station misst etwa 34 x 49 × 52 cm. Das Gehäuse folgt dem eher einfachen, funktionalen Aufbau der Qrevo-Reihe und setzt voll auf Kunststoff. Die Verarbeitung ist dennoch ordentlich. In der Station stehen Behälter für 4 l Frischwasser und 3,5 l Schmutzwasser bereit. Der Staubbeutel der Absaugstation fasst 2,7 l. Frischwasser und Schmutzwasser sind von oben zugänglich. Der Staubbeutel sitzt hinter einer Abdeckung an der Vorderseite. Nach der Reinigung saugt die Station den Staubbehälter des Roboters automatisch ab, füllt Wasser nach und wäscht die beiden Mopps mit bis zu 75 °C heißem Wasser. Danach werden sie mit 45 °C warmer Luft getrocknet. Das reduziert den manuellen Pflegeaufwand deutlich. Im Gegensatz zu deutlich teureren Modellen ist die Station aber weniger wartungsfrei. So muss etwa die Waschwanne gelegentlich von Hand gereinigt werden. Eine automatische Dosierung von Reinigungsmittel gibt es ebenfalls nicht. Die Einrichtung ist einfach. Nach dem einfachen Zusammenbau der Station und dem Einsetzen der Wischmopps wird der Roboter über die Roborock-App mit dem WLAN verbunden. Der QR-Code für die Einrichtung befindet sich unter dessen oberer Abdeckung. Anschließend erstellt der Roboter mit seinem Lasersensor eine Karte der Wohnung, die anschließend angepasst werden darf. Die Roborock App gehört weiterhin zu den umfangreicheren Lösungen am Markt. Die anfangs automatisch erstellten Räume lassen sich teilen, zusammenführen und weitergehend bearbeiten. Bereiche können gezielt gereinigt oder über Sperrzonen und virtuelle Grenzen ausgeschlossen werden. Für einzelne Räume sind unterschiedliche Reinigungsabläufe möglich. Auch die Reinigung von Teppichen kann separat konfiguriert werden. Für das Wischen stehen unterschiedliche Intensitätsstufen und Streckenführungen zur Auswahl. Im Modus „Gründlich+“ fährt der Qrevo S Pro langsamer und legt seine Bahnen enger. Zusätzlich dürfen Nutzer die Wassermenge in 30 Stufen einstellen. Wer bestimmte Räume intensiver behandeln möchte, kann entsprechende Abläufe in der App speichern. SmartPlan 2.0 übernimmt auf Wunsch einen Teil dieser Entscheidungen automatisch. Das System passt Einstellungen unter anderem an Raum und Reinigungssituation an. Das funktionierte im Test gut. Für die Einbindung ins Smart Home unterstützt der Qrevo S Pro Amazon Alexa, Google Home, Siri Kurzbefehle und Matter. Damit lässt sich der Roboter auch in herstellerübergreifende Automationen einbinden. Der Lasersensor auf der Oberseite vermisst die Umgebung und dient der Kartenbildung und Routenplanung. Die Hindernisvermeidung setzt zusätzlich auf das sogenannte Reactive-Tech mit strukturiertem Licht. Das aufwendigere StarSight-System einiger Spitzenmodelle, das die Umgebung mit 3D-Sensoren erfasst und Hindernisse zusätzlich per RGB-Kamera erkennt, kommt beim Qrevo S Pro nicht zum Einsatz. Die Navigation des Qrevo S Pro funktioniert trotzdem gut. Der Roboter fuhr im Test auch enge Bereiche gezielt an und bewegte sich zuverlässig zwischen Möbeln und sonstigen Einrichtungsgegenständen. Die klassische LiDAR-Navigation liefert nachvollziehbare und weitgehend systematische Fahrwege. Bei der Objekterkennung überzeugt uns das Ergebnis nicht abschließend. Größere Gegenstände wie Schuhe, Socken oder Spielzeug werden zwar meist erkannt und umfahren, bei herumliegenden Kabeln oder anderen kleinen Gegenständen wie Katzenspielzeug oder Legosteinen klappt das oft nicht. Auch bei Schwingstühlen hielt sich der Roboter im Test länger als nötig auf und fuhr sich vereinzelt daran fest. Bei Türschwellen liegt die Grenze bei rund 2 cm. Ein anhebbares Fahrwerk wie bei teureren Modellen besitzt der Qrevo S Pro nicht. Roborock nennt eine maximale Saugkraft von 18.500 Pa. Damit liefert der Qrevo S Pro auf Hartboden überzeugende Ergebnisse. Staub, etwas Sand oder anderer loser Schmutz wird nahezu restlos aufgesaugt und später in der Reinigungsstation entsorgt. Auf Teppich fällt das Ergebnis deutlich schwächer aus. Während dünne Teppiche und Läufer mit Teppich-Boost noch ganz ordentlich gesäubert werden, hat der Roboter auf hohem oder dichtem Flor deutlich mehr Probleme und mehr Schmutz bleibt zurück. Das machen manche ähnlich teure Konkurrenten besser. Immerhin: Bei Haaren schneidet die Kombination aus Vollgummi-Hauptbürste und Seitenbürste mit Verhedderungsschutz besser ab, echte Haarverwicklungen gab es im Test nicht. Zum Wischen verwendet der Qrevo S Pro zwei rotierende Mopps. Sie drehen sich mit bis zu 200 Umdrehungen pro Minute und auf Teppichen hebt der Roboter beide Mopps um 10 mm an. Bei kurzen Teppichen funktionierte das in Tests zuverlässig, bei hohem Flor reicht der Abstand dagegen nicht immer aus. Im Gegensatz zu teureren Modellen kann der Qrevo S Pro die Mopps nicht automatisch in der Station zurücklassen. Auf normalem Hartböden ist die Wischleistung ordentlich. Frische Kaffee- und Saftflecken werden klaglos aufgenommen, sofern es sich nicht um zu viel Flüssigkeit handelt. Eingetrocknete Senf- und Zahnpastareste verschwanden weitgehend, aber nicht vollständig – bei Flüssigkeiten und hartnäckigen Flecken sind Wischrollen einfach besser. Eine klare Schwäche ist die Randreinigung. Weder der rechte Mopp noch die Seitenbürste lassen sich nach außen fahren. Entlang von Wänden und besonders in Ecken kann deshalb ein schmaler ungereinigter Bereich zurückbleiben. Das ist im Jahr 2026 ein klarer Ausstattungsnachteil, da mittlerweile auch günstigere Modelle ausfahrbare Reinigungselemente bieten. Im Qrevo S Pro steckt ein Lithium-Ionen-Akku mit 5.200 mAh. Die maximale Laufzeit wird mit bis zu 180 Minuten angegeben. Eine vollständige Ladung dauert weniger als vier Stunden. Im Alltag reicht das abhängig von der Beschaffenheit der Reinigungsfläche eher für 80 bis 100 m², danach fährt der Roboter zum Zwischenladen zurück zur Station. Die UVP des Roborock Qrevo S Pro liegt in Deutschland bei 589,99 Euro. Aktuell bekommt man das Modell je nach Farbvariante und Anbieter schon ab 390 Euro. Der Roborock Qrevo S Pro konzentriert sich auf die Kernfunktionen eines Saug- und Wischroboters. Die LiDAR-Navigation arbeitet zuverlässig, die App bietet viele Einstellungen und die Station nimmt dem Nutzer mit automatischer Staubentleerung, Wasserbefüllung, Moppwäsche mit bis zu 75 Grad und Trocknung bis 45 Grad viel Arbeit ab. Besonders für Hartböden ist der Qrevo S Pro eine gute Wahl, auf der Fläche saugt und wischt der Roboter gut. Auf höherem Teppich überzeugt das Modell dann weniger und seine Randreinigung ist mangels ausfahrbarer Seitenbürste und entsprechendem Wischpad etwas enttäuschend. Das gilt auch für die Hinderniserkennung, zumindest, wenn man von den teureren Modellen des Herstellers besseres gewohnt ist. Unterm Strich bleibt ein ordentlicher Roboter, allerdings kann er sich gegen ähnliche bepreiste Modelle der Konkurrenz nicht wirklich durchsetzen. articles.content: 본문 자동차 [현장] 1700개 용접점에 가는 길도 AI가 찾는다…현대차 공장의 미래 유하영 기자 수정 2026-10-19 00:40 펼침 0:00 Your browser does not support the audio element. ‘자율운영공장’ 비전…데이터 합쳐 AI가 생산 최적화 2032년 이후 신공장에 휴머노이드 본격 적용 추진 핸드 그리퍼 기술…로봇 팔이 ‘사람 손’처럼 와이어 집어 16일 경기 의왕시 현대차·기아 의왕연구소에서 이인환 제조SI기술개발2팀 책임매니저가 로봇 경로 자동 생성 기술에 관해 설명하고 있다. 현대자동차그룹 제공 자동차 차체를 향해 뻗은 로봇 팔이 조금씩 움직였다. 용접 지점에 가까워질수록 길을 더듬듯 멈췄다가 움직이기를 반복했다. 가상공간에서 생성한 이동 경로를 실제 차체 위치에 맞춰 보정하는 과정이었다. 앞서 연구진이 차체 위치를 일부러 틀어놓자 카메라 센서가 이를 인식해 화면 속 가상공장에 반영했고, 인공지능(AI)이 새로운 이동 경로를 생성했다. 보정이 끝나자 이번에는 멈춤 없이 매끄럽게 움직였다. 지난 16일 경기 의왕시 현대차·기아 의왕연구소에서 선보인 로봇 경로 자동 생성 기술의 시연 장면이다. 자동차 차체에는 1700개 이상의 용접점이 있다. 기존에도 용접 작업 자체는 자동화됐지만, 로봇이 각 용접점까지 이동하는 경로는 현장 엔지니어가 일일이 설정해야 했다. 이날 기술을 소개한 현대차·기아 제조SI기술개발2팀 이인환 책임매니저는 “사용자가 전혀 개입하지 않고 이동 경로를 자동 생성하는 기술”이라며 “초기 생산라인 구축과 양산 준비 기간, 투입 비용을 절감할 수 있다”고 설명했다. 현대차·기아는 2027년 6월까지 이 기술 개발을 마치고 양산공장 적용을 검토할 계획이다. 로봇 경로 자동 생성 기술을 시연 중인 모습. 현대자동차그룹 제공 현대차·기아가 19일부터 사흘간 의왕연구소에서 여는 ‘이포레스트 테크데이 2026’은 이처럼 AI와 소프트웨어를 활용한 미래 제조 기술을 선보이는 자리다. ‘이포레스트’는 현대차·기아의 스마트공장 브랜드다. 올해로 7회째를 맞은 행사에서는 200여 건의 제조 신기술을 전시한다. 현대차그룹이 궁극적으로 지향하는 것은 ‘자율운영공장’이다. 사람과 로봇이 협업하고, 인공지능이 데이터를 바탕으로 스스로 학습하고 판단하며 생산 과정을 지속해서 최적화하는 공장을 뜻한다. 단순히 사람 없이 돌아가는 무인공장이 아니라, 위험하고 반복적인 작업은 로봇에 맡기고 사람은 공정 판단과 품질 개선 등에 집중하도록 하겠다는 구상이다. 이를 실현하기 위한 핵심은 데이터의 연결과 통합이다. 기존에는 공장마다 생산과 품질, 설비 관리 시스템 등을 개별적으로 개발·운영하면서 데이터와 개발 역량이 분산되는 문제가 있었다. 현대차·기아는 이를 해결하기 위해 데이터 수집·관리 체계와 개발 환경을 표준화하는 ‘소프트웨어 중심 공장’(SDF) 구축을 추진하고 있다. 한 공장에서 개발한 제조 기술과 소프트웨어를 다른 국내외 공장에도 신속하게 적용하기 위한 기반을 마련하겠다는 것이다. 이날 선보인 제조 특화 인공지능 에이전트 ‘폴라리스’는 데이터 통합이 실제 현장에서 어떻게 활용될 수 있는지 보여줬다. 담당자가 “어제 ‘차도의’ 주요 결함에 대해 알려줘”라고 음성으로 요청하자 폴라리스는 이를 ‘차체·도장·의장’ 공정으로 해석해 결함 분석 결과와 시각화 자료를 제시했다. 엔지니어가 여러 시스템을 오가며 찾아야 했던 정보를 인공지능이 분석하고, 보고서로 만들어 공유하는 기능도 갖췄다. 폴라리스는 지난 9월 울산 전기차 공장에서 시범 운영을 시작했다. 조립 공정에서는 사람의 손길이 필요했던 작업까지 로봇에 맡기려는 시도가 이어지고 있다. 이날 전시장에서는 사람 손을 닮은 ‘핸드 그리퍼’를 장착한 로봇 팔이 전기차 부품의 고정용 와이어를 손가락으로 집거나 움켜쥐어 빼낸 뒤 아래 회수 상자에 내려놓았다. 기존에는 작업자가 직접 하던 일이다. 현대차·기아 제조SI기술개발2팀 유지훈 책임매니저는 “사람의 손을 모사할 수 있는 핸드 그리퍼를 적용해 다양한 형태의 부품을 다루는 기술을 개발하고 있다”며 “아직 개발 초기 단계이지만, 추후 조립 자동화 고도화의 핵심 기반이 될 것”이라고 설명했다. 실제 공장 적용 일정이 구체화한 기술도 있다. 작업자가 허리를 숙여 19개의 클립으로 자동차 문 아래쪽의 마감재인 ‘도어 가니시’를 고정하던 작업을 로봇이 대신하는 기술이다. 현대차·기아는 이를 2027년 12월 기아 광주1공장에 적용할 예정이다. 현대차·기아가 선보인 고난도 자동화 기술인 바디 웨더스트립 및 도어 가니시 자동 장착 시연 모습. 해당 기술은 작업자의 부담을 줄이고 조립 품질을 높이기 위해 개발됐다. 도어 가니시 자동 장착 기술은 2027년 12월 기아 광주1공장에 적용할 예정이다. 현대자동차그룹 제공 완성차 품질 검사에도 인공지능을 활용한다. 터널형 외관검사 장치에서는 차량 한 대당 약 5천장의 초고해상도 이미지를 촬영하고, 인공지능이 결함의 위치와 크기를 분석해 화면 속 차체 전개도에 표시했다. 현대차·기아는 외국산 시스템에 의존하던 검사 기술의 광학계와 알고리즘, 하드웨어와 소프트웨어를 자체 개발해 내년 7월 기아 화성 이보 플랜트(EVO Plant) 웨스트 공장에 적용할 계획이다. 현대차그룹은 싱가포르 글로벌 혁신센터(HMGICS)를 미래 제조기술의 실증 거점으로 삼아 미국 메타플랜트 아메리카(HMGMA), 울산 전기차 공장 등 신공장과 기존 글로벌 공장으로 기술을 단계적으로 확대할 계획이다. 2030년에는 싱가포르 글로벌 혁신센터에서 가상환경 기반 자율화 제조시스템을 고도화하고, 2032년 이후 미래 신공장에는 휴머노이드 로봇과 전면적인 자율화 기술을 본격 적용한다는 목표다. 다만 이날 공개된 기술들은 이미 시범 운영 중인 것부터 양산 적용을 준비하거나 초기 개발 단계에 있는 것까지 상용화 수준이 제각각이다. 자동화 확대가 현장 노동자의 역할을 어떻게 바꿀지도 과제다. 최영태 현대차·기아 제조솔루션본부 이포레스트센터장(상무)은 “사람은 더 안전하고 가치 있는 일에 집중하고, 데이터와 인공지능은 공장을 더욱 유연하고 지속 가능하게 운영하도록 돕는 제조환경을 만드는 것이 목표”라고 말했다. 유하영 기자 yhy@hani.co.kr

articles.title: PETA's 'Gen G' Play Utilizes Audience Tech Voting
articles.content: Why every audience vote matters in PETA’s ‘Gen G’ play Oct 17, 2026 1:00 PM PHT Angel Camille Dio Listen to this article Powered by  Speechify Already have Rappler+? Sign in to listen to groundbreaking journalism. INTERACTIVE. A scene from the play 'Gen G: GG na ‘To! Project GG Facebook page INFO The choose-your-own-adventure format of ‘Gen G’ forces the audience to stay fully immersed in the story, with the active, live-voting feature directly dictating the fate of the characters AT A GLANCE The interactive theater show 'Gen G: GG na ‘To' engages a Gen Z audience by allowing them to make real-time choices that influence the story's outcome, reflecting the complexities of decision-making in their lives. The narrative centers around characters navigating rising floodwaters in Balangay Gen Zones, symbolizing community and the shared systems that shape their realities. The production aims to empower youth by highlighting the importance of their choices and encouraging them to actively participate in shaping their future, with performances continuing until December 2026. This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors . The show begins with the Joker asking the audience to help guide the story toward a satisfying ending. Most of the crowd belongs to the younger generation, or the digital natives widely known as “Gen Z.” “Gen G began by listening to young people talk about how they make these choices,” said Ian Segarra, director of the interactive theater show Gen G: GG na ‘To! “Through our conversations with them, what emerged is that choosing is rarely simple. Our decisions are shaped by our families, friends, fears, responsibilities, circumstances, and the systems we live in. What seems like the wrong choice from the outside may feel like the only choice available to us.”  Organized by the Philippine Educational Theater Association (PETA) and Move to Change Foundation, Inc. (M2C), Gen G: GG na ‘To allows viewers, particularly the younger audience, to make choices as they watch the play. Inspired by what Filipinos commonly say, “ Kabataan ang pag-asa ng bayan (The youth is the nation’s hope),” the story features  the characters Dex, Achi, Chloe, and Sid, all fighting for survival amid rising floodwaters in Balangay Gen Zones. “At the heart of Gen G is the image of the Balangay — a vessel built to carry people together. It becomes a symbol of community and of the systems we inherit and build together,” Segarra said. “We may not have created the world we are given, but we are constantly participating in how it is maintained, shaped, and transformed.” Perhaps more than entertainment, Gen G is a live exercise in democracy. The show relies on real-time choices from the crowd, which, Segarra noted, resulted in unpredictable choices during the play. This, he shared, also provided the production team with fresh insights.  “There are surprising answers. Merong mga hindi namin ine-expect na makikita nila, na nakita nil a (We see things we didn’t expect them to catch),” said Segarra.  “It’s surprising and sometimes it’s also enlightening. Na parang, ‘Ah okay, ganito pala talaga…ganito mag-isip ang mga kabataan ngayon (Ah okay, so this is how today’s youth actually think) . ”  This choose-your-own-adventure setup forces the audience to stay fully immersed in the story, with the active, live-voting feature directly dictating the fate of Dex, Achi, Chloe, and Sid as they navigate the rising waters. Since the cast must adapt to the audience’s decisions, the story flow changes with every single performance. “I thought that theater is very powerful in evoking the emotions or evoking the capacity and potential of the youth. Hence, we considered to mount this play with PETA,” said Liza Abaya, founder of Move to Change Foundation, Inc. The cast, all Gen Zs themselves, makes the play even more relatable to the young target audience.  On stage, they portray characters with clashing personalities and conflicting ideas — forcing the audience to carefully weigh options during crucial decision-making moments. Ultimately, the characters have to make choices to achieve their common goal: saving their Balangay. “In our practice, we cannot prescribe it. We will always pick it up from the audience,” said PETA president Melvin Lee. “If they will bring up a specific issue, the audience has to resolve it and come up with their own stand about a specific issue. Us artists, we cannot prescribe it for the audience.”  Zoe Damag, the cast member who plays the Joker, emphasized how this interactive approach empowers both the actors and the students. “When students perform and engage, they come alive and realize their true capabilities. You are forced to research and deeply understand your reality, because you cannot portray a character — or make a choice — with half-baked knowledge,” Damag said in Filipino.  Despite the different choices within the story, the casts come in well-prepared to execute different scenarios every show, having rehearsed all possibilities.  “​That’s why it’s difficult at times, challenging at times, but it’s beautiful also because you get to understand how the young people also react to what is [in front of them],” Damag said. Gen G will continue to tour schools and universities until December 2026.  As the play respects the young audience’s real-time decisions, it also allows them to realize the weight of their choices. “What if the future of our community depended on the choices we make today?” EO Masilungan, M2C’s executive director, asked.  “​Young people saw something that mattered, and they decided to do something about it. And that is change-making.” – Rappler.com Angel Camille Dio is a Rappler intern studying BA Journalism at Polytechnic University of the Philippines. articles.title: AI Agentic Reasoning Advances with Latent Space
articles.content: --> (cs) [Submitted on 13 Oct 2026] Title: Hybrid Reasoning Agents Authors: Jiaru Zou , Yunzhe Qi , Sirui Chen , Federico Bianchi , Shang Zhu , Pan Lu , Jingrui He , James Zou View a PDF of the paper titled Hybrid Reasoning Agents, by Jiaru Zou and 7 other authors Abstract: How can we build an agent that thinks beyond human language, yet still acts through it in the external environment? Modern LLM agents still reason and interact through text, while latent reasoning offers an efficient internal medium but lacks native tool access and reasoning transparency. We bridge these two directions with Hybrid Reasoning Agents (HybridAgents), which dynamically navigate between latent reasoning and text-based interaction throughout a unified generation process. Architecturally, a lightweight HybridLink enables seamless transitions between text and latent modes, while the agent's continuous working memory preserves lossless hybrid context across multiple turns. These designs preserve tool-integrated agentic capabilities while making latent thoughts directly inspectable. Building on this architecture, we further develop dedicated post-training algorithms for hybrid reasoning: HybridSFT stabilizes tool-integrated hybrid generation by teaching the backbone to coordinate with HybridLink, then HybridRL scales reasoning by learning when to think in latent space and when to act through text. We evaluate HybridAgent at 3 model scales across 11 benchmarks covering mathematics, science, medicine, search, and agentic reasoning. Compared with frontier LLM Agents and agentic frameworks spanning both text-based and latent methods, HybridAgent consistently improves performance by 10.4%, while delivering 35.5%-54.7% token reduction, 1.8x-2.6x faster inference, and 2.7x-3.7x cost savings. articles.content: 본문 과학 수면 중 ‘분홍 소음’이 뇌 청소 촉진한다 곽노필 기자 수정 2026-10-19 09:41 펼침 0:00 Your browser does not support the audio element. 곽노필의 미래창 깊은 수면 단계서 부드러운 소리 들려줬더니 뇌 노폐물 제거하는 뇌척수액 흐름 활발해져 수면 중 적절한 시기에 빗소리처럼 부드러운 분홍 소음(핑크 노이즈)을 들려주면 뇌 척수액의 흐름이 더욱 활발해지는 것으로 나타났다. 픽사베이 잠을 자는 동안 우리 몸은 움직이지 않고 휴식을 취하지만, 몸 안에서는 건강을 지키기 위한 생리적 과정이 활발하게 진행된다. 몸의 사령탑인 뇌의 통제에 따라 각종 호르몬이 온몸을 순환하며 낮 동안 여러 활동을 하느라 지치고 손상된 조직을 복구하고 면역 체계를 재정비한다. 동시에 뇌 스스로는 낮에 쌓인 기억을 차곡차곡 정돈하고, 뇌척수액을 이용해 낮 동안 쌓인 젖산이나 독성 단백질 등의 노폐물을 씻어내며 다음날을 준비한다. 수면 중 뇌 세포에 달라붙어 있는 노폐물을 씻어내는 작업은 글림프 시스템이 담당한다. 잠을 자는 동안 세포 사이 공간이 넓어지면서 뇌를 둘러싸고 있는 뇌척수액이 뇌 안으로 들어가 노폐물을 걷어내고 다시 빠져나온다. 더러워진 곳에 물을 뿌려 오염 물질을 씻어내는 것과 같다. 미국 매사추세츠공대(MIT) 연구진이 수면 중 수면 중 적절한 시기에 분홍 소음(핑크 노이즈)을 들려주면 뇌 척수액의 흐름이 더욱 활발해지는 것을 발견해 국제학술지 ‘사이언스 중개의학'(Science Translational Medicine)에 발표했다. 연구진은 분홍 소음의 이런 효과를 이용하면 알츠하이머병 치매를 유발하는 독성 단백질 배출이 촉진될 수 있을 것으로 기대했다. 분홍 소음 실험 결과. A는 기능적 뇌자기공명영상 촬영 부위(노란색 점선), B는 각 부위에서 뇌척수액이 유입되는 신호가 나타난 부위(빨간색 화살표), C는 청각 자극 전후에 뇌척수액 유입 신호가 어떻게 흘러가는지 보여주는 시계열 그래프, D는 분홍 소음(Stim, 파란색 선)을 들려줬을 때 약 5~7초 뒤(**표시 부분) 뇌척수액 유입량이 유의미하게 증가하는 걸 보여준다. 사이언스 중개의학 서파가 정점 이르렀을 때 분홍 소음 자극 분홍 소음이란 우리 귀에 들리는 모든 소리 가운데 주파수가 높아질수록, 즉 음이 높아질수록 소리가 작아지는 소리를 말한다. 고주파(고음) 에너지가 저주파(저음)에 비해 약하기 때문에, 묵직하고 부드러운 소리가 난다. 잔잔한 빗소리나 멀리서 들려오는 폭포 소리가 이에 해당한다. 심신 안정, 집중력 향상, 숙면에 도움을 주는 것으로 알려져 있다. 연구를 이끈 로라 루이스 교수는 앞서 기능적 자기공명영상(fMRI)을 이용해 수면 중 뇌척수액의 흐름을 측정하는 방법을 알아내고, 뇌척수액 흐름이 깊은 수면(비렘수면)과 관련된 뇌파인 서파(slow wave)와 긴밀하게 연동돼 움직인다는 사실을 밝혀낸 바 있다. 서파는 느리고 진폭이 큰 뇌파를 가리키는 말이다. 잠이 깊을수록 서파의 진폭도 커진다. 서파 수면은 잠든 직후, 즉 밤의 전반부에 가장 많이 나타나고, 새벽으로 갈수록 그 비중이 줄어든다. 이번 연구는 그 후속으로, 뇌파를 조작해 뇌척수액 흐름을 개선할 수 있는지 알아보는 작업이었다. 연구진이 건강한 성인 14명을 대상으로 실험한 결과, 수면 중 서파가 정점에 이른 시점에 50밀리초(ms) 길이의 짧은 분홍 소음을 들려줬을 때 서파 진폭이 커지면서 뇌척수액의 흐름이 더 활발해지는 것으로 나타났다. 더 커진 서파가 혈관 수축과 확장을 촉진해 뇌척수액이 뇌 안으로 더 많이 들어가도록 펌프 역할을 한 것이다. 이는 뇌척수액이 노폐물을 품고 다시 뇌 밖으로 나가는 흐름도 촉진한다는 걸 시사한다. 일반적으로 유입과 유출은 균형을 이루기 때문이다. 루이스 교수는 분홍 소음의 효과를 아이가 그네를 탈 때 적절한 순간에 그네를 밀어주면 그네가 더 멀리 가는 것에 비유했다. 연구진은 분홍 소음을 이용한 뇌척수액 흐름 촉진이 불면증이나 알츠하이머병 같은 신경퇴행성 질환에도 효과가 있을지 알아볼 예정이다. 픽사베이 치매 물질 배출 촉진 기대…실용화 기기 개발중 그러나 이를 증명하는 과정은 쉽지 않았다. 뇌파와 뇌척수액 흐름을 동시에 측정해야 했는데, fMRI에 사용하는 자기장이 뇌파 검사(EEG)를 방해했기 때문이다. 연구진은 이 문제를 해결하기 위해 fMRI의 방해를 100밀리초 이내에 재빨리 제거하는 초고속 뇌파 신호 처리 방식을 개발했다. 아울러 서파가 정점에 이르는 시기를 예측하는 알고리즘도 개발했다. 덕분에 분홍 소음을 가장 효과적인 시점에 정확히 전달할 수 있었다. 나이가 들수록 서파가 발생하는 깊은 잠은 줄어드는 경향을 보인다. 연구진은 다음 단계로 분홍 소음을 이용한 뇌척수액 흐름 촉진이 불면증이나 알츠하이머병 같은 신경퇴행성 질환에도 효과가 있을지 알아볼 예정이다. 논문 제1저자인 조슈아 레빗 박사는 “알츠하이머병 치매는 아밀로이드 베타나 타우 같은 독성 단백질의 뇌 축적이 일부 원인이 돼 발생하기 때문에 뇌 노폐물 제거가 매우 중요하다”며 “뇌 노폐물 배출 기능을 촉진할 수 있다면 독성 단백질 축적을 억제하는 데 도움이 될 수 있을 것”이라고 말했다. 연구진은 연구에만 그치지 않고 실용화에도 나섰다. 이번 연구에서 확인한 것을 토대로, 수면 중 적절한 시점에 청각 자극을 전달해 뇌척수액 흐름을 돕는 머리띠형 장치를 개발하는 중이다. *논문 정보 Closed-loop auditory stimulation in phase with slow waves during sleep enhances cerebrospinal fluid flow in humans.
